findings.description: Every session in the same checkout overwrites the same .run/context-class file. Start a standard-context session, then a long-context session: the second session replaces the first session's recorded class, and --show explicitly trusts that shared record.
findings.failure_mode: The standard-context session subsequently reads 'long' and follows thresholds ten times larger than its required standard thresholds. Atomic replacement prevents partial reads but does not prevent one session from replacing another session's configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the class under a session-specific identifier and make both --show and the context-discipline instructions resolve the current session's record.

findings.cross_file_justification: loa-status.sh display_context_line (in diff, truncated) and tests/unit/context-class.bats CC-9 invoke the hook after `cd $T` without `--root`; ROOT is derived from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, so when $T sits inside any git work tree the hook reads and writes the enclosing repo's .run/context-class, not $T's.
findings.description: ROOT defaults to the git top-level rather than the caller's working directory or an explicit `--root`. Any caller that relies on cwd (the CC-9 test, `/loa` run from a nested checkout, a bats tmpdir created under a work tree) silently targets the wrong repository's `.run/` directory. The reviewer reports CC-9 failing and a record being written into the enclosing repo, i.e. the test suite both fails and has a side effect on the developer's checkout.
findings.failure_mode: CI red on context-class.bats CC-9; running the suite overwrites the developer's real .run/context-class; `/loa --show` in a nested repo reports/writes the parent repo's class.
findings.suggested_fix: Have loa-status.sh and the tests pass `--root "$ROOT"` explicitly, and change the default to prefer an already-resolved root (e.g. `${LOA_ROOT:-$(git -C "$PWD" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)}`) so the cwd of the caller, not of the hook process, decides. In the bats test, create $T outside any work tree or `git init` inside it.

findings.description: The class fails open: every unknown-model path (no `.model` in the SessionStart payload, jq or yq missing, catalog lookup miss, hook-guard swallowing stdin) yields `long`, which the regenerated context_discipline include in 10 skills turns into 20K/50K/30K/150K thresholds. Claude Code's SessionStart payload does not reliably carry a model id, so a 200K-context session gets a 150K session threshold (75% of its window) unless the operator knows to export LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS=standard. This is a 10x loosening of the previous universal 2K/5K/3K/15K rule for exactly the users who most need the tighter one.
findings.failure_mode: Standard-context sessions blow past compaction with no synthesis to NOTES.md; the recorded basis=default gives no hint anything went wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Either default to `standard` when the model is unknown (fail closed, basis=default) and let the long class require positive evidence, or surface a one-line warning via --line/`/loa` when basis=default so the operator can set LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS.

findings.description: .run/context-class is a single per-checkout file but the class is a per-session property. Two concurrent Claude Code sessions on one checkout with different models (or one with LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS set) last-writer-win the record; `--show` then reports the other session's class and the skills' context-discipline block follows the wrong thresholds. The atomic mv prevents torn writes but not the semantic race.
findings.failure_mode: A standard-class session reads `long` written by a sibling session and runs with 10x thresholds; `/loa` output disagrees with the session's real model.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the record by session (e.g. `.run/context-class.<session_id>` using the payload's session_id, with the un-suffixed file as a fallback) or embed the session_id in line 2 and have --show warn when it does not match the current session.

findings.description: `--root`, `--model` and `--catalog` do `shift 2`. When the option is the last argument, bash's `shift 2` with $#==1 fails and shifts nothing; with `set -u` but no `-e` the while loop re-enters with the same `$1` forever. `loa-context-class.sh --model` (or a caller that expands an empty variable into `--model "$X"` after word-splitting) hangs the hook, and as a SessionStart hook that blocks session start until the harness times it out.
findings.failure_mode: Infinite loop / hung SessionStart hook on a trailing valued option.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && { VAR="$1"; shift; }` per option, or `shift 2 || break`.

findings.description: `timeout 2 cat` uses GNU coreutils `timeout`, which is absent on stock macOS (the framework's cross-platform-shell.md / KF-012 class). There the command fails, `|| true` swallows it, payload is empty and MODEL is never derived from the hook input, so model-based classification is dead on macOS and every session is `long` (see DISS-002). Nothing in the record distinguishes this from a genuinely absent `.model`.
findings.failure_mode: Silent total loss of model detection on macOS; always basis=default.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard with `command -v timeout` and fall back to plain `cat` (stdin is closed by the harness) or `read -t 2 -r -d ''`, and record `payload=none` in the metadata line when nothing was read.

findings.description: The stubs (helper-scripts.md, constructs-integration.md, and per the reviewer trajectory-evaluation.md) say they keep 'the old path and its anchors stable', but every heading was removed, so any `helper-scripts.md#mount-loash`, `constructs-integration.md#exit-codes`, etc. link now resolves to a 4-line file with no matching anchor. helper-scripts.md also dropped its 'Related Protocols' links.
findings.failure_mode: Existing deep links into the five moved protocols land on a stub with no anchor; the stub's own claim is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the 'anchors stable' claim, or keep the original H2 headings in the stub each followed by a one-line pointer to the same heading in the reference/ copy.

findings.cross_file_justification: The regenerated context_discipline include (in diff) no longer mentions session-continuity.md, yet the protocols-summary row for reference/session-continuity.md still lists `skills' context_discipline` as a loader.
findings.description: Stale 'Loaded by' column introduced in the same PR that removed the reference. protocols-summary.md explicitly positions itself as the authoritative index that replaced a drifted table, so shipping it already drifted undermines its purpose. The header also still says 'one row per file' while the five stubs at the old paths plus five reference/ copies now exceed the row count.
findings.failure_mode: Doc drift; agents following the index look for a reference that does not exist in the include.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the row's loader to `structured-memory.md pointer; context-engineering.md` and adjust the header to note that stub files are not listed separately.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff shows sibling protocols (grounding-enforcement.md, synthesis-checkpoint.md) link to each other with bare relative paths; the five files moved into reference/ (truncated in this view) very likely carry the same relative links (e.g. `structured-memory.md`, `citations.md`, `tool-result-clearing.md`), which now resolve to nonexistent `.claude/protocols/reference/<name>.md`.
findings.description: Moving a markdown file one directory down breaks every relative link inside it unless they were rewritten to `../<name>.md`. The visible diff rewrote inbound links to the moved files but there is no visible evidence the outbound links inside the moved files were updated.
findings.failure_mode: Dead cross-protocol links from the reference/ copies.
findings.suggested_fix: Grep the five reference/*.md files for `](` and bare `.md` paths and prefix with `../` (or use repo-absolute `.claude/protocols/...`); add a link-check to validate-ck-integration.sh or check-loa.sh.

findings.cross_file_justification: tools/check-prompt-budget.sh (in diff, truncated) lowers the CLAUDE.loa.md limit to 9216 B while the regenerated file is 9199 B; the constraint tables inside it are regenerated from constraints.json `why` strings edited in this diff.
findings.description: 17 bytes of headroom against a hard budget limit on a generated file. Any future one-word change to a constraints.json `why` string, or the next version bump in the managed header, flips CI red with no relation to the change being made. The protocols total is reported to sit permanently above the new warn line, making that warning noise from day one.
findings.failure_mode: Brittle CI: unrelated constraint edits fail the prompt-budget check; a permanently firing warning trains people to ignore it.
findings.suggested_fix: Set the limit with a few hundred bytes of slack (or make it ceil(current*1.05)), and either raise the protocols warn line above the current total or exclude protocols/reference/ from the sum since it is explicitly outside the prompt budget.

findings.cross_file_justification: _context_window_of reads the live .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml; the tests CC-3/CC-6 reportedly assert against live catalog entries (claude-opus-5 = 1M, haiku-4-5 = 200K, a tiny alias) rather than a fixture.
findings.description: Tests coupled to catalog data will break on routine model-catalog maintenance and conversely will not catch regressions in the resolver itself. The hook already accepts `--catalog FILE`, so a fixture is cheap.
findings.failure_mode: Spurious test failures on catalog updates; alias/provider resolution regressions masked.
findings.suggested_fix: Point CC-3/CC-6 at a minimal fixture YAML via `--catalog` covering: alias → provider-prefixed target, direct model, ≤200000 and >200000 windows, and a miss.

findings.description: A 54-file change that adds a SessionStart hook, a new per-checkout state file, a two-class threshold regime that alters agent behaviour in 10 skills, moves five protocols and lowers prompt-budget limits ships with no CHANGELOG entry. Operators upgrading via update.sh get a new hook and new `.run/` file with no release note explaining LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS.
findings.failure_mode: Undocumented behaviour change for downstream mounts; no discoverable pointer to LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an Unreleased CHANGELOG entry covering the hook, `.run/context-class`, LOA_CONTEXT_CLASS, the protocol moves/stubs and the new budget limits.
